name: Sheep milk
summary: Sheep milk is the rich milk of the ewe, drunk fresh or made into yoghurt and cheeses such as feta. This page lists what people say it does and what writers in ancient Greece and Rome believed; each claim can be checked against the research when you choose.
inIt: The UK food table (CoFID) measures raw sheep's milk at 93 kcal, 5.4 g of protein, 5.8 g of fat, 5.1 g of sugars (lactose), 170 mg of calcium, 0.32 mg of riboflavin and 0.6 µg of vitamin B12 per 100 g. Whole pasteurised cow's milk in the same table has 63 kcal, 3.4 g of protein and 3.6 g of fat. The table does not measure the fat droplets or the milk sugars other than lactose.

A review says sheep milk has high concentrations of proteins, fats, minerals and vitamins compared with the milks of other domestic species, and that its make-up suits products with added probiotics or prebiotics.

lore.who: Ancient Rome (Pliny the Elder, about 77 AD)
lore.belief: Pliny wrote that ewes' milk is sweeter and more nutritive than cows' milk but not so well suited to the stomach, because it is more oleaginous (oily) than any other.

sources.title: Pliny the Elder, Natural History 28.33 (fifty-four medicinal uses of milk), Bostock and Riley translation, 1855
sources.author: Pliny the Elder

lore.who: Ancient Rome (Pliny the Elder, about 77 AD)
lore.belief: Pliny said that where the intestines have been rubbed raw by strong purgatives or by dysentery, cows' milk or ewes' milk is the best milk to use.

sources.title: Pliny the Elder, Natural History 28.33 (fifty-four medicinal uses of milk), Bostock and Riley translation, 1855
sources.author: Pliny the Elder

lore.belief: The Hippocratic writer taught that a barley drink (cyceon) made with milk is nourishing, and that one made with sheep's milk is astringent, while one made with goats' milk is more laxative.

sources.title: Hippocrates, Regimen II, chapter 41 (cyceon), Jones translation, Loeb Classical Library vol. IV, 1931 (Internet Archive scan)
sources.author: Hippocratic Corpus (W. H. S. Jones, translator)

tableFoods.label: 1 small glass of raw sheep's milk (about 150 ml, 155 g)

processing: The UK food table lists sheep's milk raw only. Raw dairy is a safety question: in a review of dairy outbreaks in Canada and the United States from 2007, 20 outbreaks involved unpasteurised products (449 confirmed cases, 124 hospitalisations, five deaths).

whoShouldBeCareful.note: A report describes 28 children who had severe allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, to goat and sheep milk products although they tolerated cow's milk, and it says that many children allergic to cow's milk also cannot tolerate goat's or sheep's milk. If you or your child have a milk allergy, talk to your doctor or allergist before trying it.

whoShouldBeCareful.with: Pregnancy or a weakened immune system (raw milk)
whoShouldBeCareful.note: A review of dairy outbreaks in Canada and the United States says pregnant women and people with weakened immunity should be made aware of foods at high risk of Listeria. If this applies to you, talk to your doctor or midwife before drinking raw milk.

unknowns: Whether drinking sheep milk changes any health outcome: this page found no human trial of it; the review cited is about its make-up and its use in foods.
How much sheep milk's make-up varies with breed, feed and season: the table has a single raw entry.
